newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Citic Pacific results fail to surprise.
newsitem.headline: HK's Citic Pacific results fail to surprise.

text.p: There were no surprises up CITIC Pacific Ltd's sleeve on Wednesday when it posted a hefty gain in 1996 profits of HK$6.86 billion (US$886.3 million), up from HK$3.073 billion in 1995, analysts said.

The rise was due to exceptional gains of HK$3.298 billion from the disposal of a 3.85 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and the sale of a 17.66 percent interest in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd.

Both were reported in CITIC Pacific's interim profits. Analysts were forecasting profits of between HK$6.38 billion and HK$6.99 billion for the year ended December 31, 1996, from the red chip conglomerate.
ING Barings analyst Mark Simpson said the relatively tight range of analysts' forecasts showed the company had kept the market well informed.
Simpson said he had forecast net profits of HK$6.72 billion.
Steven Thompson, chief analyst at Nikko Research Center, said he had only been surprised by CITIC Pacific's interest expense and tax figures.
"They (the profits) were better than I was expecting. (CITIC) got me on their interest expenses and on the taxation side. Both of those were lower than I had expected," he said.
CITIC Pacific said net interest expense fell to HK$41 million, from HK$313 million, thanks to a placement of 120 million shares in January 1996.
Its tax bill fell by HK$97 million to HK$418 million after the removal of Hongkong Telecom from the associated company category.

"I don't see anything special (in the result) other than that their interest expense was basically quite a bit lower than last year," said an analyst who declined to be named. "Otherwise, everything was up to expectations."
The analyst expected net profits of HK$5.1 billion in 1997, although he said he might make a slight upward revision in light of the 1996 results.
Salomon Brothers' Anil Daswani said the company had a range of options to keep up profit momentum in 1997.

It might sell small investment properties that were not key parts of its strategy or even its big development in Quarry Bay on Hong Kong island, Daswani said. Shrinking its Hongkong Telecom stake further was another option, he said.
Daswani said he expected 36 percent growth in attributable profits in both 1997 and 1998, excluding exceptionals.
China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) would contribute some substantial earnings in 1997, and this would grow even more in 1998, said Daswani.
CITIC Pacific holds a 20 percent stake in CLP, one of Hong Kong's two power generator.
Daswani also expected better performance from trading arm Dah Chong Hong as the Hong Kong market improved this year.
CITIC Pacific's has interests in aviation, trading, motor vehicle distribution and servicing, infrastructure, investment holding, warehousing and distribution, and property investment.
